items.name: High Knees and Butt Kicks Line
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free. In a small room, do every movement in place for 20 seconds instead of over a distance.
items.setup: Mark a start line and a line 20 yards away (or 20 feet for a small space). Players line up shoulder to shoulder with an arm's length between them.
instructions: Easy jog down and back once to get warm.
High knees down: drive each knee up to hip height with quick, light feet and pumping arms. Walk back.
Butt kicks down: heels flick up toward the backside with the knees pointing at the ground. Walk back.
Side shuffle down facing one way and back facing the other, staying low with feet never crossing.
Finish with one run at three-quarter speed, tall posture, eyes up.
In a small space, do each movement in place for 20 seconds with a 10-second rest.
items.reps: 1 round of each movement over 20 yards, down and back
items.parentTip: Do it with your child. Laughing through high knees together is the point; form matters less than getting warm and having fun before the real work.
safety: Start with the easy jog; never sprint cold.
Check the lane for toys, holes, or wet spots before the first run.
items.funVariation: Animal Line: call an animal for each trip, such as 'giraffe' for tall high knees, 'kangaroo' for two-foot hops, or 'crab' for side shuffles, and let the kids invent the next one.

items.name: Arm Circles: Small to Big
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free; works anywhere there is room to hold the arms out to the sides.
items.setup: Players stand in a circle or a line with enough room to stretch both arms straight out to the sides without touching anyone.
instructions: Arms straight out to the sides: 10 tiny circles forward, then 10 medium, then 10 big slow circles that brush the ears.
Repeat backward: 10 tiny, 10 medium, 10 big.
Arm swings: swing both arms forward and back like a giant walking, then cross them in front of the chest and open wide, 10 each.
Shoulder shrugs: lift both shoulders to the ears and let them drop, 5 times.
Trunk twists with hands on hips, 10 each way, feet planted.
Finish with 5 slow shadow throws with no ball, thumb down and up to the L, finishing at the opposite hip.
items.reps: About 60 circles total plus swings, shrugs, and twists
items.parentTip: Big circles should be slow. Fast, flailing circles do not warm the shoulder; slow full ones do. Count out loud together so the pace stays easy.
safety: Keep an arm's length from the next player so swinging arms do not collide.
Stop any movement that pinches in the shoulder and move on to the next one.
items.funVariation: Helicopter Takeoff: the group starts with tiny circles and whispers, growing the circles and the noise until the coach calls 'takeoff' and everyone jumps once, then starts over backward.

items.name: Walking Lunges With a Twist
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free. In a small room, do stationary lunges in place, alternating legs, with the same twist.
items.setup: A line 10 to 15 yards long on grass or any flat surface. Players stand at the start line an arm's length apart.
instructions: Step forward into a lunge: front knee over the ankle, back knee hovering an inch or two above the ground, chest tall.
At the bottom, reach both arms out and twist the upper body slowly toward the front leg, then back to center.
Push off the front foot and step into the next lunge with the other leg. Walk the whole line this way.
Walk back easily and repeat once, this time twisting toward the opposite side of the front leg to feel the difference.
Add a knee hug between lunges for a second trip: stand, pull one knee to the chest for two seconds, then lunge.
Keep the pace slow; this is a stretch and a balance drill, not a race.
items.parentTip: Watch the front knee: it should point straight ahead, not cave inward. If balance is wobbly, shorten the step; a shorter lunge done well beats a long one done badly.
safety: Flat surface free of holes and loose balls.
Back knee hovers; nobody bangs a knee on concrete.
items.funVariation: Follow the Leader: the leader adds one silly element to each lunge, such as a clap at the bottom or a superhero pose on the twist, and the line copies it.

items.name: Skips and Shuffles
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free. In a small space, skip in place and shuffle two steps each way.
items.setup: Two lines 20 yards apart (20 feet in a small space). Players spread out along the start line.
instructions: Regular skips down the line with big arm swings, walk back.
Power skips: drive the knee up and reach for the sky with the opposite arm, trying to get height, not distance. Walk back.
Side shuffles down facing one way and back facing the other, low and quick, feet never crossing.
Backpedal down with short quick steps and the chest over the toes, then turn and jog back.
Carioca (grapevine) for ages 9 and up: cross one foot in front, then behind, moving sideways with the hips turning. Walk back.
Finish with two runs at three-quarter speed, tall and relaxed.
items.reps: 1 trip of each movement down and back
cues: Feet never cross on the shuffle
items.parentTip: Skipping looks silly to some older kids. Do it with them; a parent skipping badly makes it safe for everyone to try.
safety: Backpedal only on a surface checked for holes and loose balls, with a spotter calling 'stop' at the line.
Start easy and build; the first trip is never a sprint.
items.funVariation: Coach Says: the coach calls the next movement mid-trip ('shuffle!', 'skip!', 'backpedal!') and players switch instantly. Anyone who switches on a call that did not start with 'coach says' does a silly victory dance.

items.name: Shoulder and Wrist Wake-Up
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free; a wall is handy for the wall slides but not required.
items.setup: Players stand an arm's length apart. This drill comes after the body is already warm from jogging or skipping and before the first throw.
instructions: Wrist flicks: arms out in front, flick the wrists up and down 15 times, then make 10 wrist circles each way.
Elbow bends: arms out to the sides at shoulder height, bend at the elbows so the hands touch the shoulders and straighten, 10 times.
Shoulder blade squeezes: arms out to the sides, pull the shoulder blades together like pinching a pencil between them, hold two seconds, release, 10 times.
Goalposts: make an L with both arms (elbows at shoulder height, hands up), then rotate the hands forward and down to point at the ground and back up, slowly, 10 times.
Trunk twists with arms crossed on the chest, 10 each way.
Finish with 5 slow shadow throws, thumb down, up to the L, through to the opposite hip, then the first real throws start from one knee at short distance.
items.reps: 1 round of each movement, about 4 minutes
items.parentTip: This is the part of the warm-up most kids skip. Watch the goalposts: the elbows should stay at shoulder height while the hands rotate, which is the same L the throw needs.
safety: All movements are slow and in a comfortable range; stop anything that pinches.
This replaces nothing; the one-knee easy throws still come before any hard throwing.
items.funVariation: Robot Warm-Up: players do every movement like a robot with sound effects, and the coach 'oils' any joint that is moving too fast by tapping a shoulder to slow it down.

items.name: Easy Jog and Walk It Out
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free. In a small room, march in place for one minute, then walk slow laps around the room.
items.setup: Any open loop: around the bases, around the yard, or around the room. Everyone moves in the same direction with space between players.
instructions: Jog very slowly for one to two minutes, slow enough to talk in full sentences the whole time.
Drop to a walk for one minute, swinging the arms loosely and shaking out the hands.
While walking, take five big slow breaths in through the nose and out through the mouth.
Finish walking to the spot where the stretch or the talk will happen.
On a team, jog the bases in order as a group at talking pace, then walk the last base path.
items.reps: 1 to 2 minutes jogging, 1 to 2 minutes walking
items.parentTip: If your child can not talk while jogging, the jog is too fast. The cool-down is where the body slows down, so slower is better than faster.
safety: Keep the pace slow enough to talk; this is not conditioning.
Make sure players have water available at the end.
items.funVariation: Story Jog: the group tells one story one sentence per person while jogging. The story must end exactly when the jog does.

items.name: Light Stretch Circle
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free; works on grass, a mat, or a carpet.
items.setup: Players stand or sit in a circle after the easy jog with an arm's length between them. A coach or parent leads and counts; everyone holds each stretch gently with no bouncing.
instructions: Arm across the chest: hold the throwing arm across the body with the other hand for 15 to 20 seconds, then switch arms.
Overhead reach: reach both arms up and lean gently to one side for 15 seconds, then the other.
Quad stretch: standing on one foot (hold a partner's shoulder), pull the other heel toward the backside for 15 seconds, then switch.
Hamstring: sit with one leg out and reach toward the toes with a flat back for 15 seconds, then switch.
Calf: hands on a partner's shoulders or a wall, one leg back with the heel down for 15 seconds, then switch.
Finish with three slow breaths and a gentle shake-out of the arms and legs.
items.reps: Each stretch held 15 to 20 seconds per side, 1 round
items.parentTip: Stretches should feel like a gentle pull, never pain. Count out loud so your child relaxes into the hold instead of rushing.
safety: No bouncing and no pushing into pain; a stretch that pinches is released right away.
This is general cool-down movement, not treatment for an injury; any pain that lasts is a conversation with a doctor.
items.funVariation: Stretch Leader: a different player leads each stretch and picks the count-down word, counting 'baseball, baseball, baseball...' or the team name instead of numbers.

items.name: Best Thing You Did Today
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free; it is a conversation.
items.setup: Players sit or take a knee in a circle, or a parent and child sit together on the grass, after the stretch. Gear is already put away so nobody is fidgeting with a glove.
instructions: The adult asks one question: 'What is the best thing you did today?' Every player answers in one sentence, including the adult.
Answers must be about effort or something learned, not only results: 'I kept my elbow up' counts as much as 'I hit the target.'
The adult reflects one thing they noticed about each player that the player did not mention, in one sentence each.
Everyone names one thing to try next time, in a few words.
Close the same way every time with a team word, a high five, or a handshake so the ending feels like an ending.
items.parentTip: Answer honestly yourself, including something you got wrong, like 'I threw a couple over your head.' Kids talk openly when adults do.
safety: Keep the circle positive; mistakes are discussed as things to try next time, never as blame.
Hydrate during the talk on hot days.
items.funVariation: Secret Shout-Out: each player names the best thing a teammate did instead of their own, and the teammate has to guess who said it.

items.name: Freeze Tag: Ready Position
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free. Indoors or in a small space, play at walking speed with a smaller boundary.
items.setup: Mark a boundary with cones, jackets, or chalk about 30 by 30 feet for a team, smaller at home. One player (or the parent) is the tagger.
instructions: Review the ready position: feet wider than the shoulders, knees bent, hands out in front, eyes up.
On 'go,' the tagger chases. Anyone tagged freezes in a perfect ready position and holds it.
A frozen player is unfrozen when a free teammate crawls under their arms, or at home when the child gives the parent a high five in ready position.
The adult checks frozen players and says 'fix your knees' or 'hands out' before they can be freed.
Switch taggers every minute. Play for about six minutes.
Indoors or in a tight space, everyone moves at a fast walk with no running.
items.reps: 4 to 6 rounds of about one minute each
items.parentTip: The teaching happens at the freeze. Take two seconds to look at each frozen ready position and fix one thing with a word; the game does the rest.
safety: Set a clear boundary and keep the surface free of balls, bats, and gloves.
Walking speed only indoors or in a small space.
Tags are two-finger touches on the shoulder or back, never pushes.
items.funVariation: Coach Pitch Freeze: the tagger yells 'ball!' before tagging and the whole group must drop into ready position for two seconds; anyone standing up straight becomes a tagger too.

items.name: Sock-Ball Catch Streak
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Roll two socks into a ball. That is the whole drill, and it is safe in any room.
items.setup: Partners stand 10 to 15 feet apart with a soft ball or sock ball. On a team, make a circle of six to ten players with one or two balls.
instructions: Partners toss the ball back and forth with two-hand catches, counting every clean catch out loud.
A drop or a throw the partner cannot reach resets the count to zero.
Every ten catches in a row, both partners take one step back.
Circle version: the ball goes to anyone, and the whole group counts; add a second ball when the group reaches twenty.
Play for five minutes and record the best streak for next time.
items.parentTip: Throw so your child can catch, not so they have to work. The streak teaches soft hands and catchable throws because a wild throw costs everyone the count.
safety: Soft or sock ball only, so this is safe indoors and for the youngest players.
Keep tosses easy; this is a game, not throwing practice, and it counts as light throwing for the day.
items.funVariation: Trick Catch Round: after a streak of ten, each catch must be made a new way: one hand, under a leg, behind the back, or with eyes closed on the parent's soft underhand toss from four feet.

items.name: Shadow-Swing Simon Says
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free; no bats are used, only empty-hand shadow swings.
items.setup: Players spread out two arm-lengths apart facing the leader. No bats; every swing is a shadow swing with empty hands held together like a grip.
instructions: The leader calls baseball shapes with 'Simon says': 'Simon says show me your stance,' 'Simon says load,' 'Simon says swing and freeze your finish,' 'Simon says ready position,' 'Simon says throwing L.'
Players do the shape only when the call starts with 'Simon says.' A call without it is a trap.
Anyone caught moving on a trap does three perfect shadow swings and rejoins the game; nobody sits out for long.
The leader checks one thing each round, such as the head staying still on the swing or knees bent in the stance.
Switch leaders every minute so players practice naming the positions.
Finish with everyone doing five slow, perfect shadow swings together.
items.reps: 4 to 5 rounds of about one minute each
items.parentTip: Use the game to see which positions your child knows by name. If 'load' gets a blank look, show it once and keep playing; the game is a review, not a lecture.
safety: No bats or objects in hands; shadow swings only.
Two arm-lengths between players so swinging arms do not connect.
items.funVariation: Speed Simon: calls come faster and faster each round, and the last two players standing become the leaders for the next game.

items.name: Red Light, Green Light to First
items.equipmentFreeVariant: Already equipment-free; a chalk line, a jacket, or a crack in the driveway is the finish line.
items.setup: A start line and a finish line ('first base') 40 to 60 feet apart, 20 feet in a small space. The caller stands past the finish line with their back to the players.
instructions: On 'green light,' players run toward first base with good running form: arms pumping, eyes up.
On 'red light,' the caller turns around and every player must freeze in a balanced athletic position. Anyone still moving goes back to the start line.
'Yellow light' means jog in place with high knees until the next call.
First player to cross the finish line becomes the next caller.
Indoors or in a small space, 'green light' means fast walking only.
items.reps: 4 to 5 rounds of about one minute each
items.parentTip: Turn around quickly sometimes and slowly other times. The freeze teaches balance and stopping under control, which is exactly what a runner needs when the coach yells 'stop.'
safety: Clear lane with no balls or gloves on the ground.
Fast walking only indoors or in a tight space.
Players spread out across the start line so nobody collides on the freeze.
items.funVariation: Coach Calls: replace the colors with base coach signals. Windmill arms means run, both hands up means freeze, hands to the ground means squat into ready position.
